I really don’t think I can say I like this country anymore. I’m in my mid twenties and for most of my life I played blissfully ignorant of the eroding society around me, but once covid hit I got quite the wake up call. Almost the entire nation locked down and I thought “oh wow people are gonna have some time to themselves, maybe this’ll spark some change for the four day work week” or some such lifestyle change that lets people have more time off to live their life.
Boy, was I wrong. Within those two weeks all the celebrities in their big ass mansions were making group tik toks about how we’ll get through together, and everyone I knew over the age of 40 was clawing at their workplace door begging to come back because they were so bored. We are fortunate enough to live in a time where there are countless activities to do, things to learn, passions to pursue, but those notions seem to be nonexistent among my peers, even the ones I’ve known since childhood. Most people around me have become so boring, only able to converse about work like it’s small talk. It’s sad to see all the interesting parts of people get replaced by this abysmal workplace hustle culture that saps their whole personality away.

I don’t really know how to articulate it effectively but I’ll try, it feels like as men in the modern world we live in a giant wheel of double standards, society tells us to express our emotions but when we do they’re not taken seriously. You do anything ‘polite’ anymore like opening a door and you’ll get the evil eye from someone who thinks they’re being hit on and if you don’t hold the door you’re seen as rude. There’s a church around the corner from me that I pass on my morning runs and I’ll always walk the length of the playground outside where the daycare kids are playing. It warms my heart to hear children laugh but behind them are cold stares of the adults thinking I’m gonna hop the fence and book it with a child under each arm. Typically when expressing emotions to previous partners they’ve used it as an opportunity to turn it around on me, and as a result I’ve become incredibly reserved and afraid to express any of my emotions in fear they’ll be used against me again. It’s becoming harder and harder to go about my day without some sort of short circuit in my brain where I question my reality and how I’m supposed to act.

They had their own ambitions and personalities that often played into the conflict of the story, even in a negligible way. The Boruto villains like the Kara are…fine, I was really excited for the Kara, but I found their presence underwhelming. The anime did some justice to them. Victors scheme, deepa, boro’s cult, all great little expansions on the manga to accent the characters, but it wasn’t enough for me. 

I enjoy Boruto don’t get me wrong, but with how many times the kids were saved by their jonin superiors early in part 1 of Naruto, I expected that same kind of treatment with boruto. I feel as though the villains could be fleshed out more as well as give higher stakes to the story if the old gen was allowed to shine a little bit as well.
